profiles.name: MashedBROtato
profiles.tagline: DRIVER HAS A PERSONAL BEEF WITH THE IRONS
profiles.profile: This bag lives in two different moods: when the driver is cooking, the whole thing looks dangerous, and when the irons show up, somebody starts asking where the receipt went. The big win was a full-on heat check, but the rest of the window keeps the story messy — plenty of tee pop, plenty of self-inflicted mud on approach, and enough short-game and putting survival to keep the scorecard from catching fire completely. It’s volatile golf, not polished golf. Basically: can launch it, can scramble a little, can also turn a promising round into a demolition site in a hurry.

profiles.name: Leroy4522
profiles.profile: This is the classic grind-it-into-the-bushes-and-hope-for-a-par setup. The tee ball is usually not the villain by itself, but the approach game keeps sawing the legs off the round, which means the short game is constantly being asked to file a missing-person report on the rest of the bag. There’s occasional rescue work around the greens, but the whole profile runs on damage control and vibes, not clean contact. When the iron play goes sideways this hard, the card doesn’t need many extra invites to get ugly.

profiles.name: BigTime
profiles.profile: Tiny sample, huge amount of nonsense. The irons were basically fine, then the rest of the round arrived dressed like a problem: too many putts, not enough saving, and a short game that showed up to a fight carrying a pool noodle. One appearance can absolutely lie to you, so this isn’t gospel, but the shape is pretty clear for now — the scoring floor is living in the basement. If the putter and chipping don’t get their act together, this is going to be a lot of green-time for very little profit.
